newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE opens sharply higher after Dow rebound.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE opens sharply higher after Dow rebound.

text.p: Top British shares rose sharply on Tuesday, fired by an overnight surge in U.S. blue-chip stocks which wiped out all of Friday's heavy losses.

The FTSE 100 index was up 31.5 points at 4,043.1 by 0841 GMT, just a few points short of its closing level before "Grey Friday's' massive shake-out, which was triggered by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments on the "irrational exuberance" in financial markets.
The Dow finished some 82 points better on Monday after being up around 42 points as London markets closed.
Traders were stunned by the rapid turnaround in sentiment. On Friday, at its worst level the FTSE's dramatic fall wiped out around 25 billion pounds ($41.07 billion) from its value.
But traders said the market was underpinned by a resilient appetite for stocks: "There's too much cash around for markets to go down that far," said one, referring to Friday's tumble.
"The most sustained rallies come after a big fall as the bears get squeezed but nobody believes the rally is sustainable," the dealer added. ($1=.6087 Pound)
